questions.prompt: A controller has `[ApiController]`, and a client POSTs `{ "price": 100 }` to an action that takes `ProductDto` (where `Name` is `[Required]`). What happens?
options: The action runs with `Name = null`, and you must check `ModelState` yourself
The action returns `200 OK` with the product
The request fails with `500 Internal Server Error`
ASP.NET Core returns `400 Bad Request` automatically, without any validation code in the action
questions.explanation: `[ApiController]` enables automatic model validation: an invalid request body gets a `400 Bad Request` with structured errors before the action runs.

questions.prompt: A client sends `GET /api/products/10` to this controller. What does the response body contain?
options: Nothing; the route does not match
questions.explanation: `[controller]` becomes `products`, so the base route is `api/products`; `{id}` on `GetProduct` matches `10`, which is bound to `id` and interpolated into the string.

questions.prompt: What URL does `[Route("api/[controller]")]` give a class named `ProductsController`?
questions.explanation: `[controller]` is a token that ASP.NET replaces with the controller name without the `Controller` suffix, so the final route is `api/products`.

questions.prompt: Why do Web API controllers usually inherit from `ControllerBase` instead of `Controller`?
options: `Controller` inherits from `ControllerBase` and adds view (Razor) support, which a pure API does not need
questions.explanation: `Controller` is `ControllerBase` plus view rendering. An API that returns data uses `ControllerBase` directly; `Controller` is for controllers that also serve views.

questions.prompt: With `[ApiController]`, where does the `id` parameter of `[HttpGet("{id}")] GetProduct(int id)` come from?
questions.explanation: `[ApiController]` infers binding sources: a parameter that matches a route template token such as `{id}` is taken from the URL.
